# Licence log

**Generated — do not edit by hand.** Run `npm run check:licences` to regenerate.

This is the pre-publication due-diligence record for every asset on disk. Per **D12b**
this project imports everything each atlas offers, remains open source, and renders every
attribution its sources require; this file is how the licence position stays knowable
rather than assumed. Structure counts are read out of the shipped GLBs, not from a
hand-maintained table, so they cannot drift from what actually ships.

Project stance: **OPEN SOURCE, FULLY ATTRIBUTED, AND NOTHING IS EXCLUDED ON LICENCE GROUNDS. This project takes what each source offers, credits every one of them, and keeps an accurate account of what is inside. Commercial use is not a goal, so a non-commercial term (CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA) costs this project nothing and is NOT a reason to drop a component — the obligation it carries is attribution, and attribution is rendered in-app and embedded in every asset. Copyleft is the same: share-alike and AGPL ask for source and onward terms, which an open-source project supplies anyway. ⚠️ THE ONE THING THIS STANCE CANNOT COVER, and it is not about commerce: geometry with NO LICENCE STATEMENT grants nothing at all. Silence is not permission, so it needs written permission rather than a credit line, and `--publishable` drops it. That is a question of whether a grant exists, not of what it permits. The point of this register is therefore DILIGENT DOCUMENTATION, not gatekeeping: say precisely which licence and which permissions apply to every asset, so anyone downstream can make their own call with the facts in front of them.**.

## Assets

### `public/models/anny-adult-f.glb`

- **Licence:** Apache-2.0 (code) + CC0-1.0 (shape assets)
- **Source:** https://github.com/naver/anny — anny==0.6.0, baked by scripts/anny/bake.py
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** ANNY, a free-to-use 3D human parametric model for all ages — NAVER LABS Europe / NAVER Corporation. Apache-2.0 code over CC0 shape assets derived from MakeHuman. Cite arXiv:2511.03589. Baked to static geometry by this repository; no scan of any person was used.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** THE ONLY GEOMETRY HERE THAT IS NOT SOMEBODY'S BODY, and that is the point. Every atlas and every overlay in this register derives from a real donor — a cadaver, a scan, a segmented patient — and carries the provenance and consent questions that come with one. A parametric body is scan-free: it is generated from shape targets, so there is no donor, no consent chain and no re-identification surface. RESEARCH.md argues that is an ethical feature rather than a shortfall, and this register should say so rather than leave a blank where a donor line would be.

It exists to close D14: three of the seven atlases ship NO integumentary geometry, so the glass hull was unavailable on exactly the sources with the richest anatomy. An envelope is a skin, so the control works again. See D16.

### `public/models/ct-atlas-f.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0 (MOOSE weights) over CC BY 4.0 source CT
- **Source:** https://registry.opendata.aws/enhance-pet-1-6k/ — subject 1032, imaging-data/images/CT/1032.nii.gz; pipeline in docs/CT_ATLAS_PIPELINE.md
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** CT from the ENHANCE.PET 1.6k dataset, subject 1032 (University Hospital Leipzig contribution, CC BY 4.0); segmented with MOOSE 3.2 (ENHANCE-PET), CC BY 4.0 weights; meshed for this project.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** Built by the MOOSE pipeline from ENHANCE.PET subject 1032. THE SOURCE SCAN WAS NEVER RECORDED AT BUILD TIME — for three weeks this was the register's one unresolved entry, 'a record we failed to keep, not a party we failed to ask' (report 05), and D21's withhold machinery kept it out of the public build. RE-IDENTIFIED 18 August 2026 (D22) from three independent fingerprints, none of them memory: (1) the scan geometry — subject 1032's NIfTI header reads 287 slices x 3.0 mm = 861.0 mm z-extent, and the shipped GLB's measured anatomy span is 0.861 m to the millimetre; (2) the class census — the pipeline doc's per-model found-class counts for subject 1032 sum to 110, the GLB's exact node count, including the same 15 absent peripheral-bone classes; (3) the documentary trail — docs/CT_ATLAS_PIPELINE.md developed on enhance_1032_F.nii.gz and measured its axis codes. The dataset's own PT-details.xlsx records subject 1032 as University Hospital Leipzig: F, 81.8 y, 59 kg, 1.56 m, lung cancer, FDG-PET/CT 2009 on a Siemens Sensation 16.

⚠️ PROPERTIES THAT TRAVEL WITH IT: one 81.8-year-old oncology patient's low-dose CT — not healthy reference anatomy and not a population; skull base to mid-thigh only (861 mm), arms raised, so no skull vault, forearms-in-part, and nothing below mid-femur; the brain mask is 1 mL. Say so wherever it is offered.

⚠️ `loaded` read FALSE until 8 August 2026 and was simply stale — kept as the record of why the log once understated exposure for exactly the wrong asset.

### `public/models/eye.glb`

- **Licence:** None required — generated by this project
- **Source:** scripts/build-eye.mjs
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Structures:** 3
- **Required credit:** Schematic optical eye generated by open-twin-openXR from the published Arizona eye model (Schwiegerling). Geometry original to this project.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** THE ONLY ASSET HERE WITH NO UPSTREAM RIGHTS HOLDER. Generated from published radii, conic constants, thicknesses and refractive indices. Those are measurements, and measurements are not copyrightable expression, so the mesh is ours outright — no licence, no attribution chain, no provenance question. Crediting Schwiegerling for the parameters is courtesy and good scholarship, not a licence condition. This is the pattern to reach for whenever a structure is fully specified in the literature: generate it and own it.

### `public/models/openear-zeta.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0
- **Source:** https://zenodo.org/record/1473724
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** OpenEar library of 3D models of the human temporal bone (Sieber et al., MED-EL / University of Bern), CC BY 4.0. Surface colour baked from the same specimen's true-colour micro-slicing volume.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** The D4 texture pilot at 1/100th of Visible Human's cost (B3), and it ANSWERS D4: photographic tissue colour does survive this pipeline. The first asset here coloured by what the tissue looked like rather than by a palette we chose. Licence re-confirmed CC BY 4.0 from the Zenodo API. Specimen ZETA only, indexed and pulled member-by-member over HTTP range requests by scripts/remote-zip-index.mjs, which fetched 140 MB instead of 7.3 GB. Meshes are in RAS and the colour volume in LPS, so the shipped FlipXY.h5 — diag(-1,-1,1) — is the whole registration: 6,985 of 7,200 sampled vertices land inside the volume on non-black tissue. Placed by landmark fit rather than by eye — five structures common to it and Z-Anatomy, 1.27 mm RMS, and the same fit is what identified it as a RIGHT ear.

That is over-attribution, which marks geometry as more restricted than it is — the same error the inner-ear tag made in the other direction. The script now writes a narrower COPYRIGHT_REGIONS matching this attribution, and the built files were corrected with scripts/set-copyright.mjs.

- **Source:** https://github.com/LluisV/Z-Anatomy

- **Required credit:** Z-Anatomy - The open source atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0; incl. Anatomy of the Inner Ear by University of Dundee School of Medicine (CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0), Cranial Nerves and Foramina by University of Dundee, CAHID (CC-BY 4.0), Kidney by lissiecowley (CC-BY-NC 4.0), and white matter boundary surfaces from Brain for Blender by Anderson M. Winkler, brainder.org (CC-BY-SA 3.0); derived from BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** All seven system files imported (D12b). Per-structure component tags live in the asset's own structure table, so docs/LICENCE_LOG.md counts what actually ships. AS OF 17 AUGUST 2026 (D20) THE PUBLISHABLE AND RESEARCH BUILDS ARE THE SAME BUILD: 3,617 structures, nothing excluded. 3,607 are Z-Anatomy's own CC BY-SA 4.0 work, 8 come from two non-commercial components (4 Dundee inner ear, 4 lissiecowley kidney), and 2 — the white matter boundary surfaces of the cerebral hemispheres — are Brain for Blender (Anderson M. Winkler, CC BY-SA 3.0), restored after three weeks excluded under upstream's wrong 'University of Washington, no licence' credit. Earlier counts for the record: 3,614 while the white matter was excluded; 3,626 before a zero-vertex-part guard stopped emitting nine empty structures; 8 tagged Dundee structures before the inner-ear pattern was narrowed to exclude the middle ear.

⚠️ THERE IS A FOURTH THIRD-PARTY COMPONENT AND IT WILL NOT APPEAR IN THE COMPONENTS TABLE: 'Cranial Nerves and Foramina' (University of Dundee, CAHID, CC BY 4.0), listed in Z-Anatomy's own Resources/Models/License.txt alongside the other three. It is credited — in the attribution above, in the asset's embedded copyright, and in-app by AtlasAttribution — but it is deliberately NOT tagged per structure, because Dundee's nerve geometry and Z-Anatomy's own are not separable by name and a guessed pattern once caught the cochlear NERVE along with the cochlea (docs/PLAN_NEXT.md item 3). The table is built from tags, so a missing row there means 'not tagged', never 'not in this asset'. ⚠️ It was absent from this attribution and from build-z-anatomy.mjs's COPYRIGHT until 17 August 2026 while the interface rendered it — so the two credits that travel WITH the file were the two that omitted it, and attribution is a CONDITION of CC BY 4.0. Fixed in both, and written into the built GLBs with scripts/set-copyright.mjs rather than waiting for an FBX rebuild.

Third-party components inside this asset:

| structures | licence | component | rights holder |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 4 | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | Anatomy of the Inner Ear | University of Dundee School of Medicine |
| 4 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | Kidney | lissiecowley |
| 2 | CC BY-SA 3.0 | Brain for Blender — white (grey/white boundary) surface | Anderson M. Winkler (Brainder) |
| 3607 | CC BY-SA 4.0 | Z-Anatomy's own geometry | Z-Anatomy authors |

- **Anatomy of the Inner Ear:** Non-commercial and share-alike. Attribution is required and is rendered by AttributionBar. The sense organ only — the cochlear and vestibular NERVES and NUCLEI are Z-Anatomy’s own and are not tagged.
- **Kidney:** Non-commercial. Attribution required.
- **Brain for Blender — white (grey/white boundary) surface:** The grey/white BOUNDARY surface of the cerebral hemispheres, not white matter proper — Winkler’s own distinction, and the measured geometry agrees. Credit wording awaits his preference; the identification and the licence do not.

### `public/fonts/InterVariable.woff2`

- **Licence:** SIL Open Font License 1.1
- **Source:** https://github.com/rsms/inter/releases/tag/v4.1
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** Inter typeface by Rasmus Andersson, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
- **Embedded credit:** not checked — `asset.copyright` is a glTF field and this is not a glTF file. The required credit above is rendered in-app and recorded here; whether this format carries one internally is not read by this script.
- **Why:** Self-hosted from the official Inter 4.1 release: web/InterVariable.woff2, the COMPLETE variable font, 344 KB. Not a Google subset — a subset carries a `unicode-range`, which does not merely describe the file but restricts which characters the face may render, so anything outside it falls back to system-ui silently. Audited 29 July 2026: `->` and `~=` appear in rendered strings and Inter has both, yet the latin subset was letting the system font draw them. public/fonts/OFL.txt is byte-identical to LICENSE.txt in that release.

### `public/models/anny-grid.bin + .idx + .json`

- **Licence:** Apache-2.0 (code) + CC0-1.0 (shape assets)
- **Source:** https://github.com/naver/anny — anny==0.6.0, baked by scripts/anny/bake_grid.py
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** ANNY, a free-to-use 3D human parametric model for all ages — NAVER LABS Europe / NAVER Corporation. Apache-2.0 code over CC0 shape assets derived from MakeHuman. Cite arXiv:2511.03589. Baked to static geometry by this repository; no scan of any person was used.
- **Embedded credit:** not checked — `asset.copyright` is a glTF field and this is not a glTF file. The required credit above is rendered in-app and recorded here; whether this format carries one internally is not read by this script.
- **Why:** THE SAME MODEL AS THE FIVE ENVELOPES, SAMPLED RATHER THAN FIXED. The envelopes are five static bakes; this is ANNY's phenotype space itself, sampled at the model's own stops so the browser can interpolate between them and the six sliders are live. It backs the standalone `parametric` mode, which replaces the atlas rather than wrapping it — see D16a for why an adjustable outside over fixed organs was the wrong pairing to offer.

Registered separately from the envelopes because it is a different artefact with a different question attached: it is not a rendering of one body but the space all of them come from. The answer is the same — Apache-2.0 code over CC0 shape assets, no donor — but it is recorded rather than inferred.

## Not usable at any point

Recorded so nobody re-investigates them. These are closed by **contract or price**, which
no decision of ours can relax — unlike a licence choice, which is ours to make.

| source | instrument | why |
|---|---|---|
| zygote | proprietary, five figures | Terms forbid redistributing the content or 3D derivatives. Not reachable by D12 — this is a contract and a purchase, not a licence tier. |
| uk-biobank | material transfer agreement | Signed MTA forbids sublicensing and redistribution, and derived results return to the holder. A decision of ours cannot relax an agreement with someone else. |
| nako | material transfer agreement | As UK Biobank. |

## Action list before publishing

- [ ] **bodyparts3d**: DBCLS have not confirmed the relicence in writing. Chase it before relying on the CC BY reading for anything that matters.
- [ ] **z-anatomy**: ✅ THE DISTRIBUTION GATE IS CLEAR (D20, 17 August 2026) — for three weeks this field said the University of Washington white matter had no licence and blocked it from every served build. Resolved by asking the named source and measuring the geometry: Anderson M. Winkler (Brainder, brainder.org) denies any UW affiliation, ever; the telencephalon pair measures as his project's grey/white BOUNDARY surface (closed folded hemispheres, sphericity 0.219, exact mirrors of one source hemisphere) and is tagged white-matter-brainder at CC BY-SA 3.0, distributable inside this CC BY-SA 4.0 asset per BY-SA 3.0 §4(b); the spinal-cord tube (open, smooth, cortex-only Brainder cannot be its source) is Z-Anatomy's own and untagged. Nothing in this asset is excluded by --publishable any more. TWO THINGS REMAIN OPEN, NEITHER GATING: Winkler's confirmation from the renders sent 17 August decides the credit WORDING (docs/OUTREACH.md item 3 — if he unexpectedly disowns the pair, it reverts to Z-Anatomy's own CC BY-SA 4.0, still licensed); and upstream's licence file still carries the wrong UW credit, raised with Z-Anatomy in OUTREACH item 2 so the error stops propagating.
- [ ] **ct-atlas-f**: ✅ RESOLVED (D22). The licence chain is CC BY 4.0 end to end, each link verified at source on 18 August 2026: the Leipzig contribution to ENHANCE.PET 1.6k is CC BY 4.0 per the dataset paper (doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07218-y — only the AutoPET subset is CC BY-NC) and the AWS Open Data registry entry; subject 1032 is Leipzig per the dataset's own CT-details.xlsx and PT-details.xlsx; MOOSE 3.2 weights are CC BY 4.0. STILL TRUE: if the pipeline is ever re-run with TotalSegmentator's GATED subtasks (tissue_types, appendicular_bones, face), the output becomes non-commercial and needs its own id here. And record the subject id IN THE ASSET next time — this entry cost a forensic session because a filename was not written down.
- [ ] **htb-ct-f**: Nothing outstanding on rights. Two properties must travel with any use of it, both recorded in docs/healthy-total-body-cts-crosswalk.tsv. Labels are GROUPED -- one Ribcage rather than 24 ribs, one Spine rather than 24 vertebrae, every long bone merging left and right -- and the images being restricted means it cannot be re-segmented finer. And it is low-dose non-contrast CT, so bone is trustworthy and soft tissue is not: D10's contrast objection applies to the organ masks. ⚠️ Do not re-run this with TotalSegmentator's gated subtasks; that would make the output non-commercial and it would need its own entry.
- [ ] **biv-heart**: ✅ RESOLVED 18 August 2026 (D21) — this field said BLOCKS PUBLICATION for three weeks, on one precise question: which cohort is the bundled 'patient1' demo case, UK Biobank or CARDIOHANCE? Answered in writing by Joshua Dillon (corresponding author, Auckland Bioengineering Institute): it is a CARDIOHANCE participant, with LOCAL ETHICS APPROVAL TO SHARE ONLINE and NO RESTRICTIONS on further use. Requested credit: reference the GitHub repository and a biv-me paper — preferring the 2026 Medical Image Analysis paper (doi:10.1016/j.media.2026.104252) over the superseded FIMH 2025 one, which this register previously cited. The citation field above carries it verbatim; the attribution and the in-app credit name the cohort and the ethics basis. publishable flipped to true in src/scene/organOverlays.ts the same day. The Sunnybrook CC0 fallback (docs/INTEGRATION_CANDIDATES.md C3) is no longer needed and stays recorded only as history. What still travels with any use: ONE participant's heart, a different person from the body it sits inside, shown at their measured size — a property to state, not a rights question.
- [ ] **schematic-eye**: Nothing to verify for rights. What DOES need saying every time it is shown: it is a SCHEMATIC OPTICAL model — cornea, lens and retina only, with no sclera, iris, ciliary body, extraocular muscles, optic nerve or vasculature. Correct as optics; not a substitute for an anatomical eye, and not a donor's.
- [ ] **openear-zeta**: Nothing outstanding on rights, and the pipeline blocker is fixed: all 12 structures now carry baked photographic colour, and it renders as the `openear` organ overlay. Three properties travel with any use of it. It is ONE cadaveric RIGHT temporal bone, not a population. 71.5% of its surface has a colour source and the rest is neutral grey, because the micro-sliced block (~39.6 x 39.6 x 51.8 mm) is smaller than the scan -- grey means 'no source', never 'this colour', and the per-structure split is in the asset's own extras. And it is ~14% larger than Z-Anatomy's inner ear, left unscaled deliberately; see the note in src/scene/organOverlays.ts.
- [ ] **inter-font**: RESOLVED — no external runtime fetch remains. Verified twice: no fonts.googleapis or fonts.gstatic reference in src/ or index.html, and a full network capture of the running app shows every request on localhost with /fonts/InterVariable.woff2 served 200. Kept as a record because re-adding a CDN font link would silently reopen a GDPR exposure — LG Muenchen I (3 O 17493/20) held the IP disclosure alone sufficient. The only characters that still fall back are the emoji and geometric icons Inter genuinely lacks, which is correct: self-hosting an emoji font is neither wanted nor generally licensed.
- [ ] **npm-runtime**: Re-run the checker after any dependency bump. The one historical trap is @pmndrs/assets (CC0, fine) pulling a re-resolution of the whole pmndrs stack.
- [ ] **anny-adult-m**: THREE LICENCE BUCKETS IN ONE PACKAGE, and recording only the headline Apache-2.0 would misstate what is on screen. The code is Apache-2.0 (NAVER Corporation); the MakeHuman-derived shape assets this geometry actually comes from are CC0-1.0; a SOMA topology ships alongside under Apache-2.0 and is NOT used by these bakes. All three are declared in src/scene/bodyEnvelopes.ts and rendered in-app.

⚠️ NEVER BAKE WITH topology="smpl" OR "smplx". Both trigger a RUNTIME download of a non-commercial archive from download.europe.naverlabs.com inside download_noncommercial_data() (anny/paths.py). Because it happens at runtime rather than at install time, A DEPENDENCY AUDIT DOES NOT CATCH IT. scripts/anny/bake.py hardcodes the safe topology and exposes no flag for it — keep it that way.

NOT A MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT. The shape space is artist priors from MakeHuman, not anthropometric ground truth, so no body-composition, ergonomic or health claim may be attached. And its rest pose is not any atlas's: measured on Z-Anatomy it spans 1.124 m across the arms against the atlas's 0.646 m, so it wraps the torso and not the limbs. The interface states that; keep it stated.

- [ ] **anny-grid**: SAME THREE LICENCE BUCKETS AND THE SAME topology TRAP as the envelopes above; scripts/anny/bake_grid.py likewise hardcodes topology="anny" and exposes no flag for it.

⚠️ `race` IS DELIBERATELY NOT BAKED, though the model offers it. "african / asian / caucasian" as interpolable shape axes is a claim about human variation this project has no basis to make. `cupsize` and `firmness` are excluded separately, as body-shape controls on a rendered 3D body that is already a body-image surface. Six axes ship: gender, age, muscle, weight, height, proportions.

NOT A MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT, and the sliders make that easier to forget than the fixed envelopes did. The interface shows height, volume, mass and BMI for the generated SURFACE; mass and BMI are derived from volume under one assumed uniform density and are properties of a shape, not of a person.

THE GRID CARRIES ITS OWN TOPOLOGY (.idx), and must keep doing so. It first borrowed the index buffer from anny-adult-f.glb, whose vertices meshopt reorders during compression — so the indices numbered a different vertex array and every triangle was scrambled. Invisible on screen: positions come from the grid, so height and every slider read exactly correct, and the vertex counts matched. Signed volume exposed it (0.56 L against 51.20 L). src/scene/annyGrid.test.ts pins it and bake_grid.py asserts on it.
